records.title: AWS production task now runs a clamd sidecar, so Vault uploads are scanned there; the compose stacks (including the 'Human Testing & QA' beta stack) have no scanner and refuse every upload, and /readyz does not check AV
records.evidenceAtHead:
FIXED PART (Terraform): terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:154-160 sets CLAMAV_HOST=127.0.0.1 and CLAMAV_PORT=3310 on the api container; :167 dependsOn clamav HEALTHY; :213-270 add an essential clamav container (var.scanner_image) with the clamdcheck.sh health check, CLAMD_CONF_StreamMaxLength=100M and CLAMD_CONF_AlertExceedsMax=yes; :275-276 locals scanner_name/port. terraform/stack/variables.tf:91 pins clamav/clamav:1.4.6@sha256:57deb108...; terraform/stack/main.tf:222-227 has a memory precondition and :404 wires scanner_image. Staging and production both use ../../stack (terraform/environments/*/main.tf:43). .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:709-737 refuses a task definition with no CLAMAV_HOST, or with a loopback host and no essential, health-checked container the API waits on. securityHealth.ts:236-262: when CLAMAV_HOST is set, the boot self-test sends EICAR and fails critical (production boot refusal, header :8-10) if clamd is unreachable or misses it. uploadSafety.ts:222-236 still fails closed with 503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE when NODE_ENV=production and no scan ran.
OPEN PART: docker-compose.beta.yml (its header reads 'Beta Environment — Human Testing & QA'; NODE_ENV: production at :82) and docker-compose.yml (NODE_ENV: production at :87) have no clamav service and no CLAMAV_HOST (grep -n 'CLAMAV|clam' returns nothing for both). scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs reads only the preflight's `for VAR` list, and deploy-aws.yml:715 says CLAMAV_HOST is deliberately outside that list, so the compose gate never requires it. securityHealth.ts:225-232 still returns status 'skipped', critical:false when CLAMAV_HOST is unset, even under NODE_ENV=production. /readyz (server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts:50; header :6 lists database, schema, AnA, vault store, Redis, worker) has no AV dependency. `npm start` (package.json:40) sets NODE_ENV=production with no scanner.
records.fixedBy: 9c335454d (2026-10-01): terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:154-167 and :213-270; terraform/stack/variables.tf:79-91; terraform/stack/main.tf:222-227 and :404; .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:709-737; server/utils/virusScan.ts and server/middleware/uploadSafety.ts:190-204 (a scan over clamd's limits is refused as 422 FILE_SCAN_INCOMPLETE).
records.remaining: (1) The compose stacks docker-compose.beta.yml (the designated human-testing stack) and docker-compose.yml run NODE_ENV=production with no scanner, so every governed upload (Vault ingest, Template Library, other assertUploadSafe paths) returns 503 there, and ci:compose-boot-contract does not catch it. (2) When CLAMAV_HOST is unset, a production-mode process still boots green: the boot self-test marks AV 'skipped' and non-critical. Only the AWS deploy preflight catches this case. (3) /readyz never reports the scanner. (4) Nothing in the repo shows that the clamav image honours the CLAMD_CONF_* variables. A staging upload near the 50 MB ingest limit would settle it. Nothing records a terraform apply or an EICAR run on AWS either, and that needs the infrastructure owner.
records.severityRationale: The P0 impact, every upload refused in the AWS production environment the pilot runs on, is closed in the Terraform the pilot deploys, and the deploy preflight refuses a task without the scanner. The residual is posture and observability (boot skip when unset, /readyz blind) plus the self-host and beta compose stacks, which are not the pilot environment. It does block human testing on the beta compose stack. See blocksHumanTesting.
records.humanTestingNote: This only hits testers on docker-compose.beta.yml ('Human Testing & QA'), docker-compose.yml, or `npm start` with no CLAMAV_HOST. There, every Vault upload, and every Template Library or other governed upload, fails with 503 'File scanning is temporarily unavailable; upload rejected' (FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE). It does not occur on `npm run dev` (NODE_ENV=development only logs 'Virus scan bypassed') or on the Terraform staging stack, which has the clamd sidecar. Workaround: add a clamav/clamav:1.4.6 service to the compose file and set CLAMAV_HOST=clamav and CLAMAV_PORT=3310 on the app. Do not drop NODE_ENV=production to get around it.
records.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (git pull --ff-only, or fetch and merge, never rebase). First record the red case: bring up `docker compose -f docker-compose.beta.yml --env-file .env.beta up --build`, POST a clean PDF to /api/vault/ingest, and save the 503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE response under docs/evidence/.
2. In docker-compose.beta.yml and docker-compose.yml, add a `clamav` service on network c2c. Use the image pinned at terraform/stack/variables.tf:91 (clamav/clamav:1.4.6@sha256:57deb108fc4c72778aa83eafbca7bb7153e28c3f57c005afd38d31f16da86f23), the environment CLAMD_CONF_StreamMaxLength=100M and CLAMD_CONF_AlertExceedsMax=yes (as at terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:242-246), and healthcheck test ['CMD-SHELL','clamdcheck.sh'], interval 30s, timeout 10s, retries 3, start_period 300s. Publish no host port. On the `app` service, add `depends_on: clamav: condition: service_healthy` and the environment CLAMAV_HOST: clamav and CLAMAV_PORT: '3310'. Update each file's header comment, including the memory note: clamd holds about 1.3 GB, and briefly twice that during a reload.
3. In scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs, add a rule for every stack whose app has NODE_ENV=production. CLAMAV_HOST must be a non-empty literal naming a service in the same file. That service must have a healthcheck, and the app must depend on it with condition service_healthy (the compose equivalent of deploy-aws.yml:716-737). Add a --self-test case that removes the clamav service and asserts the check fails. Run the self-test against the HEAD compose files before step 2 and show it red.
4. In server/services/securityHealth.ts checkClamavConnectivity (:222-233): when NODE_ENV === 'production' and CLAMAV_HOST is unset, return status 'fail', critical: true, reason 'CLAMAV_HOST not set: production refuses every upload (server/middleware/uploadSafety.ts)'. Keep 'skipped' for development and test only. Extend its unit test with a production-and-unset case, which is red at HEAD.
5. In /readyz (server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts:50), add deps.virusScan. In production with CLAMAV_HOST set, send zPING\0 over TCP and expect PONG within 2 s, caching the result for at most 30 s. 'down' makes /readyz return 503. Outside production, report 'skipped'. Add a test beside server/startup/__tests__/readyz-vault-storage.test.ts with a fake listener that never answers, so 'down' is red before the change. Do not point the ECS container healthCheck at /readyz (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:181-205 explains why).
6. After terraform apply on AWS staging, run four checks: an EICAR upload gets 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED; a clean PDF gets 201; a roughly 45 MB PDF gets 201, which proves the CLAMD_CONF_StreamMaxLength override is honoured by the image; and stopping clamd leaves /readyz at 503 until ECS replaces the task. File the outputs under docs/evidence/.
records.acceptance:
- Red first: on the HEAD beta compose stack, a clean PDF to POST /api/vault/ingest returns 503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE (captured). After the change it returns 201, and an EICAR file returns 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED.
- `npm run ci:compose-boot-contract` passes on the repo, and its --self-test fails a NODE_ENV=production stack that has no clamav service or no service_healthy dependency.
- A NODE_ENV=production boot with CLAMAV_HOST unset exits non-zero and names clamav_connectivity as a critical failure. This test is red at HEAD.
- /readyz returns 503 with virusScan:'down' when clamd is unreachable and 200 when it answers PONG.
- On AWS staging, the EICAR, clean-PDF and ~45 MB results are recorded.
records.dependencies: None for the compose, boot-check and /readyz changes. The AWS apply and the EICAR and large-file proof need the infrastructure owner.

records.title: Every Authoring PDF export is still the plain-text 'Do not file' fallback (no Puppeteer driver, no Chromium); it is now labelled to the user and refused by File to Vault
records.evidenceAtHead: server/services/authoring/authoring-export.ts:499-562 renderPdf still renders through renderHtmlToPdfTracked (server/export/renderers.ts). renderers.ts:72-98 resolvePuppeteer tries 'puppeteer' and then 'puppeteer-core'. package.json:615 lists only puppeteer-cluster. `node -e require.resolve('puppeteer')` and `require.resolve('puppeteer-core')`, run at HEAD, both report MISSING. Dockerfile.optimized:52-75 installs LibreOffice, ghostscript, veraPDF's JRE and similar, but no Chromium. So getCluster returns null (:101-111), renderFallbackPdf runs (:394-395), and FALLBACK_PDF_NOTICE ('… Do not file this rendering as the formatted document.') is printed on page one (:458-482). Mitigations added since the audit (honest, but they do not fix the rendering): authoring-export.ts:46-57,560 report rendering:'plain-text-fallback'; authoring.router.ts:6674 records it on the export record, and :6684 sends X-Export-Rendering; AuthoringCreateExport.tsx:390-406 shows an error toast; authoring-file-to-vault.ts:117-119,478 refuses a PDF filing with 503 PDF_RENDERER_UNAVAILABLE ('Word (.docx) is filed with its formatting'). A LibreOffice DOCX-to-PDF pipeline exists (server/services/docx-pdf-pipeline.ts, server/scripts/docx_pdf_pipeline.py), but only AnA tools and masterDocumentBuilder call it; authoring does not. The FileToVaultDialog default is 'pdf' (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:199). Related: the eCTD leaf renderer for authored content is a pdf-lib text rendering (server/services/ectd/leaf-pdf-renderer.ts:1-19).
records.remaining: Authoring still cannot produce a formatted PDF in any environment: no tables, images, styling or real typesetting, and none of the planned bookmark, embedded-font or veraPDF work exists. No CI gate fails a production-profile export that falls back. The mitigations, labelling the export and refusing a PDF filing, make the defect honest but do not remove it. Page size is still A4 (renderers.ts:383, 466), not US Letter.
records.severityRationale: Lowered from P0. The fallback is now labelled on the file, in the export record and in the UI, and File to Vault refuses it, so there is no silent integrity exposure. A formatted DOCX path exists. But the pilot's eCTD v3.2.2 deliverables are PDFs, and Authoring cannot produce one without an off-platform Word conversion. That must be fixed before pilot users rely on Authoring for filings.
records.humanTestingNote: Export → PDF downloads a plain-text PDF. Page one says 'Plain-text rendering … Do not file this rendering as the formatted document', and the toast is an error. File to Vault with the default PDF option fails with 'The PDF renderer is not available here; this would file a plain-text rendering. Nothing was filed. Word (.docx) is filed with its formatting.' Workaround: choose Word (.docx) in Export and in File to Vault. This happens on every PDF until the renderer is replaced, so log it once, not per occurrence.
records.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (merge, never rebase). Red first: add server/services/authoring/__tests__/authoring-export-pdf-render.test.ts. It calls renderAuthoringExport({ format: 'pdf', ... }) on a fixture with two sections, one table and one heading per section, and asserts three things: rendering === 'formatted'; the extracted text does not contain FALLBACK_PDF_NOTICE; and the PDF outline (pdf-lib catalog /Outlines) has one entry per section. Gate it on `soffice` being on PATH (it is, in CI and in Dockerfile.optimized). It fails at HEAD with 'plain-text-fallback'.
2. Replace renderPdf in server/services/authoring/authoring-export.ts (:499-562) with DOCX → LibreOffice:
   - call the existing renderDocx(args, shared) (:388), which already carries the §11.50 manifest, citations, figures and the working-copy header/footer banner (:453-481);
   - write the buffer into fs.mkdtemp(os.tmpdir()) and call runDocxPdfPipeline({ inputDocxPath, outputPdfPath }) from server/services/docx-pdf-pipeline.ts;
   - read result.finalPdf, remove the temp dir in finally, and return rendering 'formatted'.
   Keep no second HTML-to-PDF path for authoring (zero duplication). renderers.ts stays for its other callers.
3. In server/scripts/docx_pdf_pipeline.py (:69-76), change `--convert-to pdf` to the writer_pdf_Export filter with JSON options: ExportBookmarks=true, ExportBookmarksToPDFDestination=true, UseTaggedPDF=true and EmbedStandardFonts=true. JSON filter options need LibreOffice 7.4 or later, so confirm the version the node:22-slim base installs. Make sure renderDocx emits section titles as HeadingLevel headings, so LibreOffice builds the outline from them.
4. Fail closed. When the pipeline throws (soffice missing, the 120 s timeout in docx-pdf-pipeline.ts:13, a non-zero exit), renderPdf throws an error with code PDF_RENDERER_UNAVAILABLE. The export route in server/routes/authoring.router.ts (~:6644-6686) maps it to 503 with the message used at authoring-file-to-vault.ts:117-119, and writes no export record claiming a rendering. Keep the guard at authoring-file-to-vault.ts:478. Remove the PDFKit fallback from the authoring path entirely, so nothing labelled 'formatted' can be plain text.
5. Have the founder choose the page size (US Letter for an FDA-only pilot) and set it on the DOCX section properties in renderDocx, so the DOCX and the PDF agree.
6. Extend the production-image smoke job (the one 20a66d955 restored) to seed and seal one authoring document. It exports PDF and fails if X-Export-Rendering is not 'formatted', if any font is not embedded (pdffonts, from poppler-utils if added, or a veraPDF profile run through the existing server/services/ectd/pdfa-pipeline.ts tooling), or if the outline is empty. Show the job failing on HEAD's image first.
7. Client: in client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AuthoringCreateExport.tsx (:390-430), show the server's message for a 503 PDF_RENDERER_UNAVAILABLE. Keep the existing fallback toast as a guard.
records.acceptance:
- Red first: the new renderer test fails at HEAD with rendering 'plain-text-fallback' (captured), and the image smoke step fails on HEAD's image.
- In the Dockerfile.optimized image, POST /api/authoring/docs/:id/export {format:'pdf'} on a sealed document returns X-Export-Rendering: formatted. The PDF has no FALLBACK_PDF_NOTICE, one outline entry per section heading, tables with their rows and columns, images present, every font embedded, and the chosen page size.
- File to Vault with PDF returns 201. The Vault copy's SHA-256 equals the artifactSha256 recorded for that filing.
- With SOFFICE_BINARY=/nonexistent and NODE_ENV=production, export returns 503 PDF_RENDERER_UNAVAILABLE and serves no PDF.
- A working-copy PDF shows the working-copy banner on every page.
records.dependencies: Founder: page size and target PDF specification (FDA PDF specifications, PDF/A or neither). LibreOffice is already in Dockerfile.optimized. Related: CAT1-09 (DOCX headers, footers and TOC flow into the PDF once it is derived from the DOCX).

records.title: SSO (SAML JIT) and SCIM-provisioned users still cannot apply any electronic signature; the only workaround is minting a local password through Forgot password, which bypasses the IdP
records.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/sso.ts:922 still creates SAML JIT users with passwordHash `saml:${crypto.randomUUID()}`. server/routes/scim.ts:840 creates SCIM users with `scim:${crypto.randomUUID()}`. server/services/part11/reverify-signer.ts:150-245 (verifySignerPassword) admits a signer only on a bcrypt match against users.password_hash; a placeholder hash never matches, and the failure is counted toward lockout (:236-237). SignerReverified.authenticationMethod is only 'password' | 'password+mfa' (:39-47). There is no IdP step-up, ForceAuthn or signing-PIN path anywhere in the module. In production an authenticator is also required (:84-87, :297-300). Every signing ceremony goes through reverifySigner: task-signoff.ts:192, mdx-qms.ts:583, ana-features.ts:2255, pccp.ts:272, governed-signed-act.ts:204, submission-sign-release.ts:260, document-lifecycle.ts:130, mdx-rbm.ts:1034,1155. So an SSO user also cannot sign a Submission Center release or a QMS record. The only code that reads saml:/scim: hashes is a compliance report (audit/compliance-reports/queries/access-review.ts:69). Workaround present at HEAD: server/routes/auth.ts handleForgotPassword (:2335-2440) has no SSO exclusion, so an SSO account can set a local bcrypt password and then sign. MFA enrolment (auth.ts:2096, :2174) needs no password.
records.remaining: Everything in the audit's fix: IdP re-authentication bound to the signature (SAML ForceAuthn, or OIDC prompt=login with max_age) or a signing PIN, the method recorded in the manifest, and a signing dialog that offers it to SSO accounts. Meanwhile the forgot-password route lets an SSO-provisioned account hold an IdP-independent local password. That is the only way such a user can sign today, and it weakens IdP control. Deprovisioning still works only through SCIM's account standing.
records.severityRationale: The pilot is sales-led with invited orgs. Invitations create password accounts (password-setup-token.ts:98-108), and those sign normally with password and authenticator. SSO-only signing is not on the pilot's critical path unless the design partner mandates SSO, in which case it becomes P0: nobody could approve, freeze, release or sign QMS records. That is the founder's open question 3 in the audit.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this with invited password accounts. A tester who signs in through SAML SSO and tries to sign (Authoring approve or freeze, Submission release, QMS) gets 'Signature rejected: password verification failed (§11.200)', and repeated tries count toward the account lockout. Workaround for testing only: use invited password accounts.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decides two things: the signing method for SSO accounts (IdP re-authentication or a signing PIN), and whether SSO-provisioned accounts may hold a local password. Record the decision in docs/LAUNCH_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (merge, never rebase).
2. Red first: add tests/db/sso-signer.dbtest.ts. It creates a user with password_hash 'saml:<uuid>' and an enrolled authenticator and drives the authoring e-sign route and submission-sign-release (submission-sign-release.ts:260) with the new credential, expecting success. At HEAD both return 401 PASSWORD_VERIFICATION_FAILED.
3. For IdP re-authentication:
   - in server/routes/sso.ts, add POST /api/sso/step-up/start {intent, recordId}. It issues an AuthnRequest with ForceAuthn="true" and a single-use nonce as RelayState;
   - in the existing ACS handler, on a step-up RelayState, verify InResponseTo, that NameID/email equals the session user, and that AuthnInstant is within 5 minutes;
   - insert a grant into a new table public.signing_step_up_grants (id uuid pk, organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL, user_id int not null, intent text, record_id text, authn_instant timestamptz, expires_at timestamptz, consumed_at timestamptz). Create it in a new IF NOT EXISTS-guarded migration added to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES before the final sweep pair (ci:migration-set-order), so the tenant RLS sweep covers it.
   For a PIN instead: add users.signing_secret_hash in a new additive migration (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS), and an Account route to set it that requires a fresh IdP sign-in plus TOTP. Hash it with bcrypt and count wrong PINs against the same lockout.
4. In server/services/part11/reverify-signer.ts:
   - add stepUpGrantId (or signingPin) to SignerCredentials;
   - add authenticationMethod values 'idp-reauth+mfa' (or 'pin+mfa');
   - when the account's hash starts with 'saml:' or 'scim:', verify the new credential instead of the password. Consume the grant atomically with UPDATE … SET consumed_at=now() WHERE consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at>now() AND user_id=$ AND record_id=$ RETURNING. Keep the account-standing, lockout and authenticator rules unchanged.
   Thread the credential through every caller listed in evidenceAtHead, and persist the derived method on the signature row and in the §11.50 manifest.
5. Client signing dialog: expose the account's auth method next to signingPostureOf (reverify-signer.ts:102-107) on GET /session and /me. Render 'Re-authenticate with your identity provider' (popup or redirect to /api/sso/step-up/start) instead of the password field for SSO accounts.
6. In the same change, refuse a local password for SSO-provisioned accounts. handleForgotPassword (auth.ts:2335) and handleResetPassword (:2453) return the same generic response but issue no token when password_hash starts with 'saml:' or 'scim:', so the IdP stays the only credential. Show this refusal failing before the change.
7. Make each of these fail and keep the failing cases as tests: a stale grant older than 5 minutes, a replayed grant, a grant for another user or record, and a password attempt on an SSO account.
records.acceptance:
- Red first: at HEAD, a SAML JIT user's sign attempt returns 401 PASSWORD_VERIFICATION_FAILED (captured in the new dbtest).
- After: the same user signs after step-up, and the signature row and export manifest show authenticationMethod 'idp-reauth+mfa' (or 'pin+mfa'). Stale, replayed and cross-user or cross-record grants are refused with 401. Forgot-password for a saml: or scim: account issues no reset token.
- The existing password-account signing dbtests stay green.
records.dependencies: Founder decisions on the method and on local passwords for SSO accounts. The design partner's SSO requirement sets the priority. The SSO lane owns server/routes/sso.ts and the IdP test tenant.

records.title: Vault versioning works now (server-assigned check-in, version list, compare, conflict offers 'upload as new version'); restore and check-out/check-in are still missing
records.evidenceAtHead:
Fixed:
- server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:133-135 accepts supersedesDocumentId (a sent version or filing is refused, :171-185).
- server/services/vault/vault-version-checkin.ts planCheckIn (:69-187) requires the head to be current in the caller's program and org, assigns the next major (nextMajorVersion :59-62), and runs again under FOR UPDATE from vault-ingest.service.ts:266.
- migrations/20260930_vault_documents_version_lineage.sql adds a lineage guard trigger and a one-successor index, and it is in the applier set (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2236).
- GET /:id/documents/:documentId/versions (server/routes/c2c/project-vault.ts:1647-1700) lists the family with SHA-256, size, uploader, lifecycle and placements.
- client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/VaultVersions.tsx:385-394 has 'Upload new version', and VaultVersionCompare is imported at :23.
- Vault.tsx:853 and :1449-1452 offer 'Upload as a new version of <title>' on the name-clash conflict, and useVaultUpload.ts:117-122 sends supersedesDocumentId.
Still missing:
- grep -i 'restore|checkout|check-out|checked_out' over server/services/vault/*.ts, project-vault.ts, vault-ingest.ts, VaultVersions.tsx and Vault.tsx finds no restore or check-out feature.
- Re-uploading a prior version's bytes is refused with 409 CONTENT_ALREADY_A_VERSION ('These exact bytes are already version N', vault-version-checkin.ts:171-184), so a prior version cannot be restored.
- Versions are sequential majors only (no minor or draft versions).
records.fixedBy: 5b9b67bbf (VR-08 check-in: vault-ingest.ts:133, vault-version-checkin.ts, migrations/20260930_vault_documents_version_lineage.sql); 15a38fbfe (VR-09 version list: project-vault.ts:1647, vault-version-family.ts, VaultVersions.tsx); 38179495f (a changed file is offered as the next version: Vault.tsx:1449-1452, useVaultUpload.ts:117-122).
records.remaining:
1. No restore: there is no route to promote a prior version to a new version with a reason, and re-uploading its bytes is refused.
2. No check-out/check-in reservation: concurrent check-ins are only serialised at commit, and the loser is refused with VERSION_NOT_CURRENT. Nothing stops a second author from working on the document while it is out for revision.
3. Only major versions exist (1.0 → 2.0), so there is no minor or draft versioning.
records.severityRationale: The dead end is gone. A revised protocol uploads as v2, its lineage is kept and enforced by the database, every version is listed and downloadable, and the conflict path offers the new-version action. Restore and check-out are standard GxP document-control features an enterprise buyer will ask for. A pilot can run without them, because downloading a prior version and re-uploading an edited copy works.
records.humanTestingNote: Uploading a revised file works ('Upload new version' in the version list, or 'Upload as a new version of …' on a name clash). A tester who tries to restore an earlier version by uploading its file again gets 409 'These exact bytes are already version N of this document. Nothing was saved.' There is no restore button and no check-out. Workaround: none for an exact restore. Download the earlier version, and an edited copy uploads as a new version.
records.acceptance:
- Red first: at HEAD, the restore route 404s and re-uploading v1's bytes returns 409 CONTENT_ALREADY_A_VERSION (captured).
- After: restoring v1 creates v3 with v1's SHA-256, superseding v2, with the reason in the audit chain. The version list shows v3 as current, with v1 and v2 retained and downloadable.
- While user A holds a check-out, user B's check-in or restore returns 409 DOCUMENT_CHECKED_OUT. After A checks in or the check-out expires, B succeeds.
- Under the runtime role, org Y cannot read or write org X's check-out row (RLS).
records.dependencies: None blocking. CAT1-15 (withdraw/obsolete) completes the lifecycle. CAT1-06 if check-out should be limited to project members.
